content.description: stablenet: 4 bp + 1 en. Binaries: default = gstable, upgrade = ${GSTABLE_UPGRADE_BIN:-gstable-hardfork}. The two names must name two files: a name is resolved on the target under one directory, so an upgrade that fell back to gstable would be the same executable and a swap onto it would measure nothing. content.description: StableNet signature compatibility: four original validators and two ENs, both restarted with a distinct upgrade binary while retaining their data. Default and upgrade binary identities must differ. The swap runs old to new, so point GSTABLE_PREUPGRADE_BIN at the older build and GSTABLE_UPGRADE_BIN at the newer one. Keys are generated because the committed preset holds five identities and this wants six.

content.description: stablenet crossing its own boho fork by restart: 4 bp run the pre-fork build, and every node is relaunched on the post-fork one well before the fork block. One chain, one build at a time — the nodes keep their databases and their work, and only the executable changes. The two builds are go-stablenet either side of the commit that added boho: ad0122af0 (the parent, which has no BohoBlock at all) and any commit after bf17c9607. The two names must name two files, because a name is resolved on the target under one directory — both falling back to gstable crossed the fork on a single build and the case passed without exercising the restart it was written for. So build both, put them on the target as gstable and gstable-postfork, or point GSTABLE_BIN and GSTABLE_POSTFORK_BIN at them. Running the pre-fork build on both sides is the control: the network cannot even start, because that build refuses a config naming a field it does not have. Used by 1 case.
